comment: War (GDD 9.3; stage 4e, ADR 0021, decisions of 2026-11-07). Every war has a goal: land (a settlement of the enemy, named when war is declared), loot (the enemy's stores) or revenge (needs a cause: an attack, an aggression or a settlement of ours they hold). goals: victimPercent and witnessPercent say how strongly the victim and everyone who knows both sides remember the aggression (relations.json aggression). Score runs from -100 to 100: a fight won gives the winner's side scorePerWin, a settlement taken scorePerSettlement more. Fighting happens in campaigns (ADR 0022: episodes with a step of campaignStepMonths): warriors of one settlement (at most sendPercent of them, at least minWarriors; a third stays home) march marchCellsPerMonth cells a month over known land to an enemy settlement, fight there (chance = their share of the strength, as in a raid), take what they can carry and go home; the commander sends one when the target is out of sight (the warriors go to look) or when the chance from what it sees now is at least minWinChancePercent; arrived, the warriors attack only with at least that chance and otherwise turn back (minWinChancePercent, sendPercent and minWarriors move to ai.json with the commander, stage 4e PR 5). Wars end by themselves in time: the world clock takes a step in the month a quiet war runs out. A war in which nobody campaigned for quietPeaceYears ends in a white peace. Weariness of a side (0..100) = months of campaigning in the war x wearinessPerCampaignMonth + percent of the side's people killed in the war x wearinessPerLossPercent; at peaceAbove the side looks for peace at once; it lowers the mood of every settlement of the side by moodAtFullWeariness at 100 (effect war_weariness in effects.json). Peace terms: when the score is at least termsAboveScore, the loser hands over the settlement a war for land was about, or else pays a one-time ransom of ransomPercentPerScorePoint percent of every store per score point from termsAboveScore up (at most maxRansomPercent); a closer war ends in a white peace. cedeWorth: what a settlement handed over is worth in score points when a side weighs terms. Arms (stage 4e PR 3, decision of 2026-11-07): armaments are the levels of arms; every warrior takes the strongest level whose technology the civilization knows and whose good (perWarrior units for one campaign, used up when the warriors set out) the settlement still has; one level needs neither (bare hands). strengthPercent: strength of a warrior with it (stone-tipped spears = 100). Defenders fight with the arms their stores allow without using them up; everyone else in a defended settlement fights bare-handed. Armies (PR 3): warriors of every own settlement at most musterCells cells from the settlement the campaign leaves from may join it (each sends at most sendPercent of its warriors); they gather there first (the muster takes the months the farthest needs to walk). An army has at most armyLimit warriors and stands on one cell per troopsPerCell warriors (eras.json; in eras 1-2 both 50, so one cell). supply: a warrior eats foodPerWarriorPerYear; a campaign sets out with food for carryFoodMonths months, at most what its warriors carry and at most supplySharePercent of each settlement's food. When it has food for fewer than convoyBelowMonths months, the nearest own settlement at most carrierCells cells away sends carriers (at most carriersPercent of its people who do not fight, each carrying carrying.perPerson of settlements.json, at most supplySharePercent of its food); they walk convoyCellsPerMonth cells a month after the army and go home when they hand over the food. A hungry campaign (no food left, loot eaten too) loses hungerMoralePerMonth morale a month, a fed one wins back fedMoralePerMonth; strength in a fight is multiplied by morale (percent); below retreatMorale it turns back; while hungry it raids the nearest known settlement of the enemy at most forageCells cells away for food and then marches on. The commander sends an army only when it can take food for at least minFoodMonths months (moves to ai.json with the commander, PR 5). A hungry campaign takes food first when it raids, and does not raid the same settlement twice in a row. Working values, to be tuned in stage 4e PR 6.
